paper.title: Smart Routing with Precise Link Estimation: DSEE-Based Anypath Routing for Reliable Wireless Networking

settings.name_in_paper: Shortest Anypath routing with unknown link delivery probabilities (DSEE-Anypath)
unmapped: Actions are anypath routes (forwarding sets per node) in a hypergraph network; cost is the nonlinear anypath cost determined by link delivery probabilities
Observations are joint reception vectors of broadcast transmissions (2^{N_max} outcomes per node); exploration sends dummy packets on all links
Regret measured in routing cost relative to a genie knowing the link probabilities
The learner knows the number of nodes N and max neighbor count N_max (used in exploration schedule)
settings.definition_quote: The task is to route a sequence of packets $m = 1, 2, ..., M $ from source node \textit{1} to destination node \textit{N} without knowing the complete network topology. Each node $ n \in \mathcal{N}$ transmits the packets in a broadcast way to every node in its forwarding set $J$. The transmission between each node and its forwarding set is characterized by a delivery ratio $p_{nJ}$ and a hyperlink cost $d_{nJ}$.

symbols.N_nodes: number of nodes in the network hypergraph
symbols.N_max: maximum number of neighbors of a node
symbols.f_T: exploration function f(T), positive, increasing to infinity
symbols.Delta_path: cost difference between the best anypath and the path selected by the policy

tuning: exploration sequence cardinality N 2^{N_max} ceil(f(t) log t)
f(t) positive monotonically increasing to infinity

source.quote: Let $ \mathcal{I}_t$ be set of times indexes from $1$ to $t-1$ where exploration has already happened. By choosing the cardinality of the exploration to be smaller than $N2^{N_{max}} \lceil f(t)\text{log}(t) \rceil $ at any given $t$, the optimal policy will have regret: \mathcal{R}_T = O(N2^{N_{max}}f(T)\text{log}(T) \Delta )

results.notes: Regret type not formally defined (difference of path costs vs genie); proof bounds expected exploitation regret. Proof is informal.

symbols.N_nodes: number of nodes in the network hypergraph
symbols.N_max: maximum number of neighbors of a node

source.quote: The regret bound can be further simplified considering $f(t)=O(\log{t})$, $\Delta = O(N)$: \mathcal{R}_T =O(N^22^{N_{max}}\log^2 T )

symbols.N_max: maximum number of neighbors of a node
symbols.Delta_path: cost difference between best anypath and selected path

conditions: wireless links between any two nodes are independent
tuning: f(t) positive monotonically increasing to infinity

source.quote: Assuming the wireless links between any two nodes are independent, the exponential number of random variables requiring observation break into a linear form, making our regret bound $\mathcal{R}_T = O(N{N_{max}}f(T)\log T \Delta) = O(N^2{N_{max}}\log^2 T)$.
